subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Expected behavior: a negative exponent is evaluated as the SBIDI reciprocal 1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS(operand-2)) -- i.e. the positive-exponent expansion of rule 2 is performed FIRST and the single division applied last, which is a different rounding sequence from repeated division. READ: NumericRenderer.Power (NumericRenderer.cs:544-553); the only standard-mode arm is `if (StandardDecimal)` -> RuntimeApi.DecPow, and the comment at NumericRenderer.cs:549 names 'r3's reciprocal for a negative exponent' for the §8.8.1.5.4 SDIDI twin implemented in CobolDec.Pow. Nothing implements the SBIDI form: ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary is absent from NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal (NumericRenderer.cs:559) and is rejected upstream by DataBinder.BindDeclarations (DataBinder.cs:318-320) with the unconditional COBOL0806 (EditionContext.cs:109 -- no permissive downgrade). No SBIDI carrier exists to divide in. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the SBIDI reciprocal leg plus a golden under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY where the single-division association is observable (e.g. 3 ** -3 vs three successive divisions). No qualifying test exists; StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported is not one (it asserts the compile FAILS). || UPHELD: rule 3 read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:8034 -- '(1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))', so the reciprocal is taken of the WHOLE rule-2 expansion, one division, and the adjudicator's rounding-sequence point is right. READ the cited comment myself: NumericRenderer.cs:546-551 is the block naming '§8.8.1.5.4 ... r3's reciprocal for a negative exponent ... The ONE runtime implementation is CobolDec.Pow' -- it is the SDIDI twin's comment and cites §8.8.1.5.4, never §8.8.1.4.4, so nothing in it can be stretched onto this row. I also read the native default arm below it (NumericRenderer.cs:554-575): it explicitly documents that a NEGATIVE or run-time exponent 'CANNOT LAND AT A COMPILE-TIME SCALE' and routes those shapes to the SDIDI carrier -- which is reachable only under {StandardDecimal, Standard}, confirming there is no standard-binary reciprocal path at all. Line refs corrected (:543 / :394 as above). I verified the closing-evidence claim by reading tests/WiseOwl.Cobol.Tests.Conformance/StandardDecimalTests.cs:111-119: StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported compiles a PROGRAM-ID unit at --std 2023 and asserts `Assert.False(ok)` plus COBOL0806 -- a rejection test, correctly refused as closing evidence. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
